final_answer: No. The trial court did not err (abuse its discretion) in disqualifying Smith Fullingham; the order should stand. Review is for abuse of discretion, typically by mandamus. Texas applies a bright-line rule for side-switching nonlawyers (legal assistants/paralegals). (1) Presumption one: a nonlawyer who worked on a matter for one side is irrebuttably presumed to have acquired that client's confidences; Jones's deposition (several hundred privileged communications, strategy meetings, drafting) makes this uncontestable, and the firm's claim that she does not recall is irrelevant. (2) Presumption two: the nonlawyer is presumed to share confidences with the new firm. That presumption is rebuttable only if the firm took reasonable, timely measures to shield her, but it becomes irrebuttable (disqualification of the firm mandatory) where the nonlawyer actually worked on the same matter at the new firm at a lawyer's direction and the lawyer reasonably should have known of the conflict (In re Columbia Valley Healthcare, 320 S.W.3d 819 (Tex. 2010); Phoenix Founders, In re American Home Products line). Here Jones worked on the Apex-Prestige matter on 13 occasions and e-filed two documents bearing her name, so the firm cannot rebut. The firm made no inquiry on hiring and imposed screening only in 2023, after she had already worked on the case; late screening does not cure. Under the most recent Texas Supreme Court decision on materially identical facts, In re Zaidi (Tex. Apr. 10, 2026, No. 24-0245), a firm must instruct the nonlawyer, at or before the time she begins work on a conflicted matter, not to work on any matter she worked on for prior employers, even if the conflict arises years after hiring; absent that, disqualification follows, and the minimal-work/not-a-side-switcher-at-hire arguments failed. Waiver: delay can waive a disqualification motion (Vaughan v. Walther, 875 S.W.2d 690 (Tex. 1994) - 6.5 months of known delay; In re EPIC Holdings, 985 S.W.2d 41 (Tex. 1998)), but the movant must have actual knowledge and have delayed unreasonably. Apex first learned in January 2023, inquired, and moved in early March 2023 (about two months), and per Zaidi, e-filing notifications listing the employee's name do not conclusively establish actual knowledge or waiver as a matter of law. Caveats: I could not retrieve the full text of Zaidi (egress blocked) and relied on search-result summaries of its holding; the firm's best arguments (limited secretarial role, lapse of time, delay) are rejected by the above authorities. Whether Apex had earlier actual knowledge from e-filing notices before 2023 is a fact question for the trial court, which resolved it for Apex.

authorities.citation: In re Columbia Valley Healthcare Sys., L.P., 320 S.W.3d 819 (Tex. 2010)
authorities.title: In re Columbia Valley Healthcare System
authorities.proposition: Legal assistant who previously worked on same matter for opposing counsel and then works on it at new firm; presumption of shared confidences irrebuttable when nonlawyer actually worked on matter; informal admonitions insufficient; firm disqualified.

authorities.title: In re Adeel Zaidi, A.K. Chagla and Prestige Consulting d/b/a Turnaround Management Group
authorities.proposition: Firm must instruct side-switching nonlawyer at or before beginning conflicted work not to work on prior matters, even if conflict arises years after hiring; e-filing notifications do not conclusively establish waiver; mandamus denied, disqualification affirmed.

authorities.title: Vaughan v. Walther
authorities.proposition: Unreasonable delay after knowledge waives disqualification complaint (6.5 months).

authorities.citation: In re EPIC Holdings, Inc., 985 S.W.2d 41 (Tex. 1998)
authorities.title: In re EPIC Holdings
authorities.proposition: Waiver analysis considers when movant learned of the basis and whether delay was explained; explained delays not waiver.

claims.text: The trial court did not err in disqualifying Smith Fullingham.
Because Jones actually worked on the same matter at the new firm, shared-confidence presumption is irrebuttable and late screening cannot cure.
Apex did not waive: it acted about two months after learning; e-filing notices do not conclusively prove knowledge.
